newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: Midwest cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower as the market continued to be pressured by a large supply of hogs coming to market, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants could range from $53.00 to $53.50.
Illinois top prices could range from $53.50 to $54.00 at plants while Indiana buyers said they expect tops at plants to range from $52.50 to $53.00.
Prices were seen pressured by sliding pork prices in the face of greater pork output.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota actual hog marketings Tuesday totaled 115,000 head, well above that day's estimate of 105,000, according to USDA. Wednesday's estimate was 110,000 head, the same as a week ago, USDA said.

USDA also estimated week-to-date slaughter through Wednesday at 1,080,000 head. The figure was not comparable with last week's 712,000-head kill because of the Labor Day holiday, but still exceeded the year-ago figure of 1,063,000.
But hog price weakness Thursday could be tempered by ideas recent declines in wholesale pork prices could energize retail interest.
That interest could be reinforced by some supermarkets' plans to feature pork in October -- which is considered National Pork Month by some in the business, sources said.
Talk that pork exports also were improving spurred ideas that a price bottom was close at hand in the cash hog market, sources said.
